# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 106 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 52 | Coptic

---

## Saying 106

Jesus said: "When you make the two one, you will become sons of man, and when you say: 'Mountain, move away!' it will move."

---

**Council Notes:**

- "Make the two one" — the unification of the divided self (cf. Saying 22: making the inner as the outer, the two as one) leads to two results: (1) becoming "sons of man" and (2) mountain-moving power.
- "Sons of man" (*shēre mrōme*): this is an ambiguous title. It could mean the messianic Son of Man (claiming the authority of the eschatological figure), or simply "human beings/children of Adam." SOPHIA preserves "sons of man" to maintain the ambiguity.
- The mountain-moving saying (cf. Matt 17:20; 21:21; Mark 11:23; 1 Cor 13:2) is here a consequence of interior unification, not of faith as a quantity. This is the distinctively Thomasine framing.
- Cross-reference with Saying 48: the two-making-peace version of this formula.
